findings.title: Default getThreads calls generate invalid SQL
findings.failure: Every existing getThreads call that omits the new SLA variables now passes an all-null serviceLevelAgreements object. The thread query produces an empty parenthesized SQL predicate, so the MCP tool fails instead of returning threads.
findings.fix: Use one nullable `$serviceLevelAgreements: ServiceLevelAgreementFilter = null` variable and pass it directly. Alternatively, make the backend normalize an all-null SLA filter to null or emit `1 = 1` rather than an empty SQL fragment.
findings.evidence: GraphQL variable coercion applies the declared null defaults before evaluating the input object, so lines 100-103 produce `{statuses:null,types:null}`. ThreadsFilter preserves that non-null object and fills updatedAt with null (packages/core-graphql/src/threads/threadsFilter.ts:59-71). buildFilters retains every non-null filter value (packages/db/src/filtering.ts:110-125), while the SLA builder returns `sql.fragment`` ` when all members are null (packages/aggregates/src/thread/threadDbFilterUtils.ts:943-947). Slonik joins do not discard an empty fragment, and threadDb inserts the resulting predicate after `AND` (packages/aggregates/src/thread/threadDb.ts:1247-1254). The old operation did not supply this object.

findings.title: The tool description documents incorrect __typename values
findings.failure: An MCP agent following the description may test for `Pending`, `Breaching`, and similar values, but those values are never returned, causing it to misclassify or overlook SLA state.
findings.fix: Document the exact values, such as `ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetailPending` and `ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetailBreaching`, or describe how to derive the status from the type name.
findings.evidence: The operation selects GraphQL `__typename`. The schema defines the union members as ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetailPending, ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetailImminentBreach, ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetailBreaching, ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetailAchieved, ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetailBreached, and ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetailCancelled (packages/core-graphql/src/schema.ts:14072-14118). GraphQL returns those exact type names.

checked_fine: All pre-existing selections, variables, routes, methods, authentication behavior, and pagination fields remain intact in the three operations.
The added union fragments and timestamp fields match the existing GraphQL schema, including nullable SLA targets and status-specific fields.
SLA enum values and the documented historical-tracker filter semantics match the existing backend filter implementation.
Summary resolution is DataLoader-batched rather than N+1, and its database query is supported by the workspace/thread/type/created-at index.
Deployment wiring, environment variables, permissions, secrets, infrastructure outputs, and exports are unchanged; the MCP image already fetches a schema containing these fields at startup.
No migrations, stored schemas, retention policies, deletes, or other data and rollback one-way doors are introduced.
Rollback only removes additive MCP response fields and filters; it does not leave incompatible persisted state.

The changed files are reachable: the Dockerfile copies the operations directory and mcp.config.yaml loads that directory. Repo-wide searches for getThreadDetails, getThreads, and searchThreads found their respective operation definitions.
No shared constants, utilities, backend resolvers, or lists were changed, so there is no additional blast radius.
No obsolete implementation, unreachable export, unused parameter, or stale runbook was introduced or left behind.
No existing repository helper can directly replace the repeated cross-file GraphQL selection without changing how Apollo MCP loads operation documents.
